story.title: SEC maps out crypto custody in new proposal that furthers its digital assets agenda - CoinDesk

facts.text: The proposal "would provide a clear regulatory framework for the custody of crypto assets, giving investment advisers and funds a compliant pathway where none existed before — and replacing the grey of uncertainty created by custody rules crafted for a bygone era,” said SEC Chairman Paul Atkins in a statement.
The latest move to advance a pro-crypto U.S. securities agenda comes the day before the exit of Commissioner Hester Peirce, who has led the agency's Crypto Task Force since its inception.
With the movement on the custody issue, the SEC has now put a checkmark in every major topic on the crypto agenda originally set out by Atkins.
According to the 760-page proposal , the SEC will allow for self-custody by advisers seeking to hold their clients' funds.
The agency is using the term "self-custody" as an asset management firm practice, not how crypto companies typically use the term.

It would first require that an adviser can’t find a qualified custodian ready to take the assets, which would likely be an unusual circumstance after the rule is implemented, and it also requires certain expertise for the investment firm to hold crypto assets.
With the movement on the custody issue, the SEC has now put a checkmark in every major topic on the crypto agenda originally set out by Atkins.

Bullish owns and invests in digital asset businesses and digital assets and CoinDesk employees, including journalists, may receive Bullish equity-based compensation.
The SEC also proposed its Regulation Crypto Asset, explaining how companies can fundraise using digital assets without running afoul of federal regulations.

Atkins said that existing custody rules "were designed to protect the assets of advisory clients and regulated funds from loss, theft, misuse, and misappropriation," but they only consider "the custody and safekeeping only of traditional assets — an untenable situation in the 21st century."
The latest move to advance a pro-crypto U.S. securities agenda comes the day before the exit of Commissioner Hester Peirce, who has led the agency's Crypto Task Force since its inception.
